author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to NATO messaging about supporting Ukraine and questions whether contemporary advertising could also be conditioning the public for the possibility of a wider European conflict. He then contrasts that suspicion with his Christian view that helping people who are suffering is a duty, while challenging the idea of using an “arbitrary war” as a route toward conscription.

From there, Russell turns to Russia, joking about the historical difficulty of invading the country and referencing Napoleon and Nazi Germany before ending with an Edward Snowden punchline.
